# [421.4] Route certified variable-duration H3 profiles through render admission and execution

## Parent
#421

## Depends on
#424 (versioned candidate profiles) and a positive route-specific #445 speed+quality operator decision. Final general-production enablement remains gated by #428.

## Execution
Autonomous engineering and test scope; no real-host certification evidence may be synthesized.

## Objective
Allow approved ShotPlans to render at eligible longer lengths through the current production job lifecycle, with precise frame-count/duration/provenance handling and fail-closed routing.

## Scope
- Refactor `packages/application/src/use-cases/map-production-duration.ts` so it maps the **requested duration + chosen certified profile identity** to grid-valid configured frames and achieved nominal duration. Keep a typed unsupported-duration result if no certified combination fits the requested duration/tolerance.
- Do not silently snap a requested 8–15s shot back to the 5000ms canonical H3 duration; no hidden fallback to a five-second profile.
- Thread explicit profile identity/capability through `PrepareSceneProductionInputsUseCase`, `EnqueueSceneProductionRenderUseCase`, production route selection/inspection, job fingerprinting, and output provenance. Do not alter underlying ShotPlan creative intent without revision/approval handling.
- Update `apps/render-worker/src/render-job-executor.ts` to validate injected frame count against the **job's exact versioned profile**, route, geometry, frame grid, optimizer/checkpoint/step identities and authentic approved provenance. Preserve current I2V vs Ref2V conditioning constraints.
- Revisit timeouts, lease/heartbeat/retry/defer, model offload, resource admissions and monitoring when a measured longer profile increases runtime; never weaken auditability or memory safety globally.
- Use actual probed media frame count/duration and output hashes for post-render validation; distinguish requested duration, nominal frame duration and measured duration. Respect assembly's exact timeline invariants and explicitly reject unresolvable mismatch rather than silently stretching.
- Add focused unit/integration tests for eligible and ineligible duration/configuration combinations, stale approvals, idempotent retry, and legacy five-second workflows.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Eligible longer frames (if any accepted by #445) execute through **explicit operator-controlled staging/acceptance**, with matching profile and provenance. General production remains disabled until #428.
- [ ] Every off-grid, uncertified or mismatched profile/route/geometry combination rejects **before GPU work** with a domain-typed error.
- [ ] No automatic fallback to 124 frames on a longer requested duration.
- [ ] Existing 124-frame production and provenance behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Output manifest and downstream duration checks use real output measurements.
- [ ] `pnpm test`, integration suite and relevant build/lint/typecheck pass; no claim of operator certification.

## Non-goals
- Change campaign planning defaults (separate #426).
- Production operator certification (separate release gate).
## Revised operator gate
Do not enable public/ordinary production queues for candidate optimization profiles as part of this implementation. #428 owns physical certification and production promotion. Include explicit negative tests: #423's 362f unoptimized I2V variant (known creative NO-GO) is not a release profile; Ref2V cannot inherit I2V eligibility. Detect silent dense-attention fallback and wrong Turbo/LoRA routing as profile mismatches.

Design document:
# Design: exact-profile H3 duration admission and execution (#425)

## Scope and evidence

Implement the software path for an approved ShotPlan to execute an explicitly selected, eligible variable-duration H3 profile in operator-controlled staging. Ordinary production remains limited to existing certified profiles; #428 owns promotion. No longer-duration eligibility or physical certification is inferred or authored by this change.

Grounding: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONTEXT.md`, ADRs 0001, 0005, 0006, 0007 and 0008; the variable-frame and continuity experiment runbooks; duration mapping, production preparation/enqueue/inspection, H3 candidate contracts/eligibility/provenance adapters, worker execution/lease handling, generation manifests, accepted-run assembly, and their tests. The effective configuration is this worktree's `.ai-orchestrator.json` only. This package is planning output; no source changes or validation runs are claimed.

## Current behavior and constraints

- #424 is present: `h3-candidate-profile.ts` binds an immutable specification digest to route, geometry, frames, workflow/model hashes, attention configuration, sampling and runner settings. `h3-capability-decision.ts` represents signed decisions and grants. `h3-candidate-registry.ts` deliberately ships an empty accepted catalog. The isolated test registry is disconnected from production exports.
- `map-production-duration.ts` already accepts an optional H3 profile argument and uses profile-scoped capabilities. However, production callers omit it; H3 recognition uses a fixed legacy alias list, and omitted/blank profiles select legacy I2V. Nearest global-grid rounding precedes the chosen profile membership check. Snap helpers explicitly return 5000ms on failure.
- `PrepareSceneProductionInputsUseCase` maps duration before selecting the approved ShotPlan route, initializes a blocked result to 124 frames, chooses fixed I2V/Ref2V keys/templates, and fingerprints achieved duration rather than retaining requested and nominal duration separately. Inspection fixes geometry to 1344x768. Enqueue also performs a separate legacy duration check before preparation, so updating preparation alone cannot admit a longer profile.
- `render-job-executor.ts` validates injected frame membership, verifies gold-master provenance, rechecks workflow hashes, verifies current creative inputs, and preserves distinct conditioning routes. Its route recognition, certification loader, profile topology and lower execution identity still assume legacy keys. An I2V alias loader fallback exists; it must remain restricted to equivalent legacy aliases.
- `ExecuteProfileRenderUseCase` explicitly rejects profile keys outside six legacy profiles. `RenderProfileKeySchema` is likewise a closed enum. Candidate provenance is a separate schema, not a legacy certification object with a different frame value.
- Existing H3 eligibility checks signatures, target host/GPU, runtime process identity, packages, node hashes and process continuity. Installed attention packages and command-line/node hints do not establish which attention implementation actually executes. Optional execution-context sampling fields also cannot substitute for checking the final submitted graph.
- The worker already hashes media and probes source bytes with frame counting and interval checks. Generation manifests distinguish `configuredMedia`, `measuredMedia` and execution wall time, but measurements alone do not enforce conformance. Configured FPS is currently inferred from baseline duration or assigned the LTX constant, which happens to also be 24.
- `GenerationManifestRepository.findVideoStemSourceByJobId` returns output reference/hash and attempt, but no measurements. Accepted-run assembly uses stored planned durations and requires their exact sum to equal the run total. FFmpeg independently probes stems and applies its existing media tolerances. These are separate invariants.
- Worker CLI defaults are 900000ms render timeout, 900000ms renewable lease and 30000ms heartbeat; the render adapter's standalone default is 300000ms. The inspection's 60-second duration ceiling is media length context, not a measured execution timeout. Longer GPU execution cannot be accommodated by changing that display constant.

## Decisions

### 1. Separate profile identity, research acceptance and execution authority

Use a resolved execution selection discriminated between legacy certified and H3 candidate profiles. Candidate selection carries exact key, version, full specification digest, immutable workflow/topology identity, route/mode, dimensions, FPS and allowed frame count. Keep legacy schemas/constants intact and add a candidate identity branch where jobs, execution and manifests actually need it; do not turn all profile strings into unrestricted identifiers.

Reuse the application `H3CandidateRegistryReader` port. Add an infrastructure reader that loads immutable operator-supplied candidate specifications plus a #445 decision envelope, validates canonical digests and detached signatures against deployment-owned trust keys, and exposes only exact rows whose speed, quality and overall verdicts pass with resolvable evidence digests. Reject duplicate/conflicting identities, absent evidence and invalid signatures. This is a read-only deployment snapshot, not a global registration API or runtime catalog mutation. The shared production catalog stays empty by default. Do not write operator records or model/profile artifacts into forbidden evidence directories.

A positive #445 row is necessary but not execution permission. Staging also requires a valid signed, time-bounded host/GPU-specific grant verified by `H3CandidateAuthorizationPort`; reuse `H3OperatorSignatureVerifier`. This implementation rejects candidate selection on ordinary admission and claim paths even if a caller supplies a production-scoped grant. #428 may later supply production certification and promotion policy through a separate change.

ADR 0008 assigns staging grants to #428 authority. Interpret this issue as implementing the grant-consuming staging machinery, not issuing a grant or assuming #445 alone authorizes execution. If no authentic accepted row or staging grant exists, the implemented deployed behavior remains typed denial; offline positive fixtures establish software behavior only.

### 2. Isolate staging while reusing the durable lifecycle

Add a durable execution scope to render jobs, defaulting existing/new ordinary jobs to production, with staging admitted only by a dedicated operator command and deployment-controlled staging configuration. Preserve `jobKind = production` for video execution; do not confuse an optimization candidate profile with a storyboard candidate job.

The operator command takes an approved staging scene, exact profile key, signed decision/grant references and request id; it invokes the same application preparation/enqueue, attempt ledger, leasing and completion services. It cannot select a profile merely by frames. Require operator-designated staging campaigns/scenes and reject attachment to an active ordinary production run. Expose equivalent inspection through the same application preparation contract so operator CLI and Review Hub diagnostics agree.

Queue claim/reclaim predicates filter durable scope. Ordinary workers cannot claim staging rows, and staging workers cannot claim ordinary rows. Control API derives permitted scope from server-owned worker/deployment configuration, never an unchecked request-body flag. Block candidate keys at generic enqueue/ordinary campaign dispatch as well as worker preflight. Persist scope in manifests and explicitly exclude staging results from ordinary campaign assembly/delivery; accepting a staging render for evaluation never promotes its profile. Existing jobs and legacy attempts retain their scope and behavior.

The additive database migration, queue filters and operator entry point are justified by the current absence of any staging discriminator: a payload-only flag would leave candidates claimable by ordinary workers. Add only the necessary scope/operation-id storage; reuse existing attempt and audit records rather than introducing a second orchestration system.

### 3. Map requested duration against the selected capability

Resolve route/profile first, then map requested duration against its exact allowed configured frames. Validate positive finite duration, finite nonnegative bounded tolerance, safe positive frame counts, FPS and `(frames - 5) % 17 === 0`. Choose the closest member of the selected allowlist within tolerance, lower count on a tie. Current profiles each permit exactly one count. Never search another profile or fall back to legacy frames after failure.

Return requested duration, configured frames/FPS and nominal frame duration `frames * 1000 / fps` separately. Preserve the existing success/error API through an adapter if callers need it, including `UnsupportedProductionDurationError`; add structured reasons for unknown identity, profile mismatch and invalid tolerance rather than generic exceptions. Mapping validates capability, not authorization: admission must separately verify authority.

At 24 FPS, 124 frames is approximately 5166.667ms, not 5000ms; 192 is 8000ms, 243 is 10125ms and 362 is approximately 15083.333ms. These latter values are examples of representable grids, not accepted release profiles. Preserve the existing 5000ms-to-124 mapping and default quantization tolerance. Do not use requested 10 seconds as proof that 240 frames is valid.

Remove snap-to-five-second behavior from admission/execution paths and prevent an invalid inspection from advertising an executable 124-frame result. Do not change campaign planning defaults or planner snap policy assigned to #426. Trace all snap callers so only explicit planning normalization can retain that behavior.

### 4. Preserve approved creative intent and bind retries to identity

Preparation checks SceneSpec revision, selected/approved ShotPlan ownership/status, routing mode, target duration, approved target frames/FPS, duration tolerance and beat bounds against the selection. A conflicting target or changed creative configuration requires existing revision/reapproval handling. Do not rewrite approved ShotPlan targets, rescale temporal beats, crop geometry or alter reference authority to make an execution fit.

Use one preparation result for inspection and enqueue, including profile capability, requested/nominal duration, scope, decision digest and grant identity. Replace duplicate H3 mapping in enqueue. Preserve Ref2V reference ordering/hashes and non-authoritative previs semantics, and I2V approved first/last-anchor requirements.

Introduce a versioned candidate production-input fingerprint covering exact specification digest/version, profile/template and workflow identity, route, dimensions, requested/nominal durations, frames/FPS, approved creative/reference inputs and authorization scope/reference. Sampling, optimizer, checkpoint and runner identity are transitively covered by the full specification digest. Keep the legacy fingerprint algorithm unchanged for existing five-second jobs and worker recomputation. Record the submitted mutated workflow hash separately from the certified template hash.

Technical retries reuse the same job, attempt id, seed, payload, selection and fingerprint; revalidate grant validity and live state on each attempt. Operator command retries with the same request id return the existing job; reuse with different canonical inputs conflicts. Use a transactional unique operation id for this new command. A changed profile/creative target creates a new authorized attempt through existing revision/approval rules, never mutates an existing queued job. A renewed grant is an explicit new authorization event, not an invisible payload replacement.

### 5. Validate exact execution before submitting GPU work

Extend worker composition to resolve candidate selections through the trusted reader and candidate provenance resolver, not the legacy alias fallback. Match durable job identity to selected specification and approved provenance. Require exact frame count/grid, geometry, FPS, mode/route, template hash, complete model hash key set, checkpoint/Turbo LoRA presence and hashes, LoRA wiring/strength, steps, sampler/scheduler, CFG/denoise, attention/sparsity, node/package revisions and runner/offload policy. Inspect the final graph after permitted prompt/seed/reference/frame injection; unchanged base-template hashes alone do not establish this.

Extend runtime observation to obtain structured effective attention/backend and sparsity evidence from the actual local ComfyUI process, bound to PID/start time and selected workflow implementation. Package presence is insufficient. For a backend that can silently fall back, require a verified fail-on-fallback implementation/runtime setting and actual backend evidence; if this cannot be observed or prevented, deny that candidate. Do not invent a ComfyUI API or accept a worker-supplied backend string as proof. Backend drift or fallback reported during execution fails the attempt and prevents accepted output publication. Recheck process continuity and grant validity immediately before submission under the shared GPU lease, without performing diffusion to test eligibility.

Use a domain/application typed admission error carrying stable blocker codes, translated to inspection blockers, HTTP conflicts and durable worker error traces. Negative cases must demonstrate zero render submission and no conditioning/GPU execution; read-only runtime probing is permitted. Preserve license routing before generation and all legacy provenance checks.

### 6. Runtime policy remains profile scoped

Attach a validated execution policy to candidate selection, sourced from authenticated operator runtime measurements and bounded deployment policy. Include render deadline, disk/RAM/VRAM budgets, offload requirement and concurrency limit; never estimate certified values by scaling frame count. If necessary measurements or a supported safe envelope are absent, reject/defer staging rather than invent them. Distinguish resource contention (bounded defer) from immutable mismatch/invalid authority (terminal typed failure).

Thread the deadline through execution/ComfyUI adapter options per job. Keep renewable leases and heartbeat cadence; an execution may outlive one initial lease interval while heartbeats renew ownership. Preserve retry limits and completion fencing. Fake-time tests cover long execution, expiry, heartbeat uncertainty, process restart, contention and repeated completion. Verify a timed-out/fenced attempt cannot release GPU capacity while its ComfyUI prompt still runs: implement targeted prompt termination/confirmed quiescence where available, otherwise keep the host unavailable until reconciled. Model unloading and lease release remain exception safe. Keep legacy policy values unchanged; no global timeout increase or concurrency/memory relaxation.

Log profile/digest, scope/grant reference, requested/nominal/measured timing, deadline, wall time, resource admission, retry/defer and mismatch code using existing worker logging/telemetry mechanisms. Do not treat wall time as media duration.

### 7. Validate measured output and preserve assembly invariants

Retain source-byte hashes, frame-counting probes, frame-interval checks and temporary-file cleanup. Before successful completion, require measured dimensions and frame count to match the exact profile, expected constant FPS and measured duration consistent with decoded frames and container precision. Reject missing/nonfinite measurements, VFR, truncated/extra frames and wrong output hash; do not replace missing measurements with configured values. Use separate explicit output/probe tolerances; the approximately 355ms creative quantization tolerance is not permission to lose frames.

Candidate manifests require requested duration, nominal configured duration, exact candidate selection/authorization provenance, submitted graph hash and paired configured/measured media tied to the same output key/hash. Keep legacy manifest fields and historical optional measurement semantics readable. Preserve top-level legacy frame/FPS semantics; do not silently redefine them as measured values. Newly rendered legacy video continues through existing measurement/provenance checks.

Extend `VideoStemSourceRecord` and adapters to expose validated measured media and execution scope for new manifests. Accepted-run admission checks these against the immutable planned durations, while FFmpeg continues to re-probe actual bytes. Preserve exact equality of the sum of stem expected durations and run total in `validateAssemblySpec`, and preserve existing stem/output media tolerances. Never replace run totals with observed totals or stretch/loop/pad footage to pass. If per-stem or aggregate measured drift exceeds existing rules, reject with a typed duration mismatch and require an explicit creative/timeline revision. Historical manifests remain readable through the existing legacy path; absence of candidate measurements or scope cannot be treated as legacy certification.

## Risks, assumptions and boundaries

1. No positive route-specific #445 decision or staging grant is supplied in the issue text or established by the empty catalog. Ship deny-by-default machinery, not invented candidate entries or certification assertions. The known #423 unoptimized 362-frame I2V tuple remains denied. A different optimized 362-frame tuple needs its own full passing decision; Ref2V never inherits I2V eligibility.
2. Active attention introspection and safe prompt cancellation are material integration risks. Implement fail-closed support for observable backends; do not label installed packages as runtime proof. Unsupported runtimes remain blocked.
3. New identity variants touch closed schemas, profile loading, manifests, license routing and execution types. Use explicit discriminated branches and boundary tests; avoid casts that smuggle candidates into legacy certification shapes.
4. Scope migration must default historical rows to ordinary production, preserve queue indexes/lease fencing and be deployed before staging workers. Rollback disables operator staging admission and drains/quiesces staging jobs before removing worker support; leave append-only attempts/manifests intact.
5. Exact campaign totals and H3 frame quantization can disagree, especially across several fractional nominal durations. This PR rejects unresolvable mismatches and documents them; it does not change campaign defaults or silently repair timelines.
6. Downstream traceability: exact profile identity, requested/nominal/measured timing and authentic provenance enable future #426 planning and #428 release evaluation. Real-provider validation, locked physical SHA runs, certification, promotion and phase sign-off are external future capabilities, not present verification gates for this PR.

# Implementation plan: issue #425

## 1. Add resolved execution selection and trusted staging inputs

Extend existing H3 candidate ports/contracts with a discriminated resolved selection and candidate execution policy. Preserve the six legacy render-profile branches and introduce explicit candidate variants in the execution/manifest boundaries that need them. Keep profile identity distinct from executable authority and keep candidate topology scoped to the selected immutable profile.

Implement a read-only infrastructure registry/decision reader using the existing canonical specification/matrix contracts and deployment-owned signature trust store. Admit only exact passing #445 rows with verified evidence references; combine with independently verified staging grants. Reuse `H3OperatorSignatureVerifier` and `H3CandidateEligibilityService`, adding the decision-verification seam rather than trusting schema parsing or caller authorization claims. Wire only into staging composition; leave shared production catalog and certification artifacts untouched.

Tests: unchanged empty production catalog; isolated positive synthetic registry; invalid signatures/digests, duplicate records, fail/unknown/missing rows/evidence; grants expired/not-yet-valid/wrong key/host/GPU/scope; known unoptimized 362f NO-GO; Ref2V denied when only I2V passes. Synthetic signing keys and records exist only in tests/temp directories and never claim hardware certification.

Validation: `pnpm vitest run packages/contracts/src/h3-candidate-profile.test.ts packages/contracts/src/h3-capability-decision.test.ts packages/application/src/use-cases/evaluate-h3-candidate-eligibility.test.ts packages/infrastructure/src/comfyui/provenance/h3-operator-signature-verifier.test.ts`, plus new reader tests; `pnpm typecheck`.

## 2. Make mapping, preparation and inspection profile explicit

Refactor `map-production-duration.ts` to map against the selected capability allowlist and return separate requested/nominal timing. Resolve H3 by structured selection, not substring guesses. Keep the legacy convenience API compatible where necessary; explicit unknown/blank candidate selection must fail. Validate tolerance and numeric/grid boundaries. Audit snap helper callers; prevent production admission or execution from normalizing a longer request to five seconds while preserving #426 planning defaults.

Resolve the approved ShotPlan and route before duration mapping in `prepare-scene-production-inputs.ts`. Replace fixed candidate keys/templates and blocked 124-frame defaults with resolved selection or a non-executable blocked result. Check target duration/frame/FPS/tolerance against approved intent, dimensions and beat bounds. Return typed errors on dispatch and equivalent blocker codes on inspection. Remove duplicate H3 checks from `enqueue-scene-production-render.ts`, retaining LTX behavior.

Extend `production-inspection.ts` and relevant inspector UI/API consumers to display scope, selected version/digest, requested duration, nominal duration and blockers without presenting staging eligibility as production certification. Keep the legacy geometry and route contracts intact; candidate geometry must equal SceneSpec and selected profile, not arbitrary new dimensions.

Tests: 5000ms -> 124 unchanged; isolated eligible 192/243/362 mappings without claiming acceptance; duration/tolerance edges and ties; NaN/infinity/negative values; unknown/off-grid/wrong route/geometry; 8–15s requests cannot return 124; invalid inspection has no executable fallback; approved timing/beat mismatch requires revision rather than mutation.

Validation: focused duration/preparation/enqueue/inspection tests and `pnpm vitest run packages/application/src/use-cases/production-input-inspector-equivalence.test.ts`; `pnpm typecheck`.

## 3. Add staging scope, admission entry point and immutable job binding

Add the next numbered additive migration for durable render-job execution scope with production default and staging constraint, and a unique staging operation id for idempotent operator requests. Update domain `RenderJob`, job queue ports, PostgreSQL enqueue/claim/reclaim decoding, control API worker claim policy and worker client composition. Scope must be checked in SQL for both queued and expired recoverable jobs. Preserve existing retry/lease logic and indexes, adjusting indexes only as required by the new claim predicates.

Add a dedicated operator staging command that consumes exact profile and signed decision/grant references, approved operator-designated staging scenes and a request id, then calls the same transactional preparation/enqueue/attempt services. Use deployment-owned scope configuration for worker/API authorization. Ordinary public enqueue/scene/campaign routes reject candidate selections regardless of supplied grants; no public candidate enable flag. Prevent staging from joining active ordinary runs or feeding ordinary assembly.

Add candidate fingerprint v2 and carry profile key/version/digest, scope, requested/nominal timing, workflow identity and decision/grant references in durable payloads. Preserve existing legacy fingerprint bytes and field interpretation. Ensure worker recomputation uses the exact pinned selection. Same request id and canonical input returns the same job/attempt; different input conflicts. Technical retry keeps seed, identity and attempt unchanged; creative rerender remains an explicit new attempt.

Tests: migration defaults; staging/ordinary claim isolation including lease expiry; unknown worker scope denial; generic route bypass denial; duplicate concurrent staging dispatch; mismatched request-id reuse; transactional rollback; retry payload persistence; stale approved plan/reference/scene rejection; unchanged legacy attempt and ordinary campaign behavior.

Validation: `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts packages/infrastructure/src/postgres/repositories/postgres-job-queue.integration.test.ts`, relevant job-route/client unit tests, and new operator/admission integration tests with the same integration config. Verify actual test paths match the checked-in include patterns.

## 4. Enforce exact profile and effective runtime before GPU submission

Update `render-job-executor.ts`, certification/profile loading boundaries and `execute-profile-render.ts` to accept the candidate identity branch through trusted resolution. Use candidate provenance collection resolution and verification without casting it into legacy gold-master schemas. Restrict the existing I2V template alias fallback to equivalent legacy identities; candidate errors never retry a five-second template. Obtain conditioning mode/topology from resolved selection.

Validate the final mutated workflow against the full specification: frames/grid, dimensions/FPS, route nodes and conditioning, checkpoint/model hashes, Turbo/LoRA routing and strength, steps/sampler/scheduler/CFG/denoise, attention/sparsity configuration, runner/offload policy and topology. Continue prompt/seed/reference-only permitted mutations and record both base and submitted graph hashes. Require all sampling identity fields for candidates instead of silently skipping absent optional comparisons.

Extend `H3RuntimeObservationPort`/`H3LiveRuntimeObserver` and eligibility evaluation with structured effective-backend evidence tied to the target process and source implementation. Inspect existing ComfyUI runtime support before choosing a probe mechanism; accept only active backend proof plus a verifiable fail-on-fallback policy for fallback-capable optimizers. Deny unsupported observation. Recheck process continuity, grant validity and selection before submitting under the GPU lease. Map mismatch failures to stable typed errors and retain license checks.

Tests: corrupt/ambiguous provenance; missing exact profile; wrong workflow/geometry/grid; graph mutation after hashing; wrong checkpoint/Turbo/LoRA/step settings; SageAttention installed but dense backend active; unsupported/unknown backend; sparsity drift; process restart and host/GPU mismatch. Assert zero queueRender calls for all preflight denials. Retain both I2V anchor and Ref2V reference-order/non-authoritative-previs suites.

Validation: focused eligibility/runtime/provenance tests, `pnpm vitest run apps/render-worker/src/render-job-executor.test.ts apps/render-worker/src/render-job-conditioning.test.ts packages/application/src/use-cases/execute-profile-render.test.ts`; `pnpm boundaries` and `pnpm typecheck`.

## 5. Carry safe profile-specific runtime policy through execution

Thread validated candidate runtime/resource policy through worker composition and render adapter execution. Keep ordinary defaults unchanged. Check disk, memory, offload and concurrency against the authenticated measured envelope using existing shared GPU lease and telemetry adapters. Missing safe policy blocks staging; contention defers with bounded retries; immutable mismatches fail without retrying another profile.

Keep heartbeat renewal independent of media duration. Address candidate deadline/fencing behavior so a timed-out or superseded ComfyUI prompt is terminated and confirmed quiescent before capacity becomes reusable; if safe cancellation is unavailable, quarantine the execution host rather than start overlapping diffusion. Preserve exception-safe unloading, cleanup and lease-release error propagation. Add structured existing-channel logs for selection, deadlines, heartbeat/retry/defer, elapsed execution and resource/mismatch outcomes.

Tests with fake timers: render longer than an initial lease with healthy renewals, expired grant at retry, missing heartbeat/lease ownership, deadline exceeded, targeted stop/cleanup failure, resource contention/defer, no overlapping GPU work, unload/release on every outcome, completion retries and unchanged legacy timeout behavior. Do not pick measured budgets in code fixtures as deployment defaults.

Validation: `pnpm vitest run apps/render-worker/src/worker.test.ts apps/render-worker/src/cli/run-worker.test.ts packages/infrastructure/src/comfyui/render-engine-adapter.test.ts packages/application/src/use-cases/execute-profile-render.test.ts`, plus affected GPU lease tests.

## 6. Enforce output conformance and expose measurements to assembly

Use the existing worker source-byte probe/hash pipeline. Add post-render conformance before successful manifest completion: exact frame count/dimensions, certified FPS/CFR, finite video duration consistent with decoded frames, paired output key/hash and defined probe/container precision. Record requested and nominal duration independently of measured duration and execution wall time. Resolve configured FPS from the profile, not the LTX constant or rounded baseline seconds.

Extend candidate generation manifest validation/assembly and storage round trips with exact selection, staging scope, decision/grant provenance and submitted graph hash; candidate measurements are mandatory. Preserve legacy schema readability and current measured/configured fields. Extend `VideoStemSourceRecord` and PostgreSQL/storage adapters with validated measurements/scope for new manifests, explicitly discriminating historical legacy records.

Update `enqueue-delivery-assembly-for-accepted-run.ts` and downstream assembly admission to compare real measurements with planned timeline expectations and reject staging candidates from ordinary delivery. Keep exact expected-duration summation and existing FFmpeg stem/output tolerances; re-probe stored bytes to verify hashes and measurements. Reject unresolvable per-stem or aggregate drift with typed errors. No automatic retiming, stretching, padding or run-total rewriting.

Tests: missing probe/count/duration, truncated/extra frames, wrong FPS/VFR/geometry, wrong hash/output key, inconsistent source-byte metadata, decimal frame duration, manifest persistence round trip, staged output delivery rejection, real FFmpeg synthetic-media measurements at variable lengths, exact-sum preservation and aggregate drift rejection. Preserve legacy five-second accepted-run and provenance tests.

Validation: focused manifest/probe/accepted-run tests; `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts packages/infrastructure/src/postgres/repositories/postgres-generation-manifest-repository.integration.test.ts`; `pnpm test:assembly` for FFmpeg integration (these files are excluded by the default and database configs).

## 7. Add lifecycle integration coverage and operator documentation

Extend `tests/integration/reference-directed-production.integration.test.ts`, production review/dispatch integration coverage and relevant PostgreSQL tests to exercise admitted synthetic staging selection -> durable enqueue -> correct scoped claim -> exact preflight -> measured manifest -> idempotent completion, with stale approval and cross-route failures. Use isolated test registries/ephemeral signatures and fake render engines, with real PostgreSQL where transaction/lease behavior matters. Prove technical retries do not add creative attempts, scope cannot be forged, ordinary candidate dispatch stays disabled and five-second jobs remain compatible. Add pinned-FFmpeg synthetic-video integration tests in the assembly suite for actual output measurements; no GPU provider or real-host certification is needed to verify software contracts.

Update the worker/operator runbook and ADR 0008 implementation notes with staging invocation, required signed inputs, deployment/rollback order, denial diagnostics, measurement semantics and #428 promotion boundary. Document unknown effective backend as an unsupported candidate, not a successful optimization. Document #426/#428 as future consumers of these contracts; do not add their real-host runs or release sign-off to this PR's gates.

## Validation and completion criteria

During implementation run focused tests after each step using the correct suite config. Before handoff run this worktree's effective tiers in order: hygiene (`pnpm check:hooks`, frozen install); isolated `pnpm format:fix`; isolated `pnpm format`; `pnpm preValidation` and `pnpm build`; then `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:bash`, `pnpm boundaries`, `pnpm check:control-plane`; then `pnpm test:db`, `pnpm test:assembly`, `pnpm test:kokoro`, `pnpm test:piper`, `pnpm test:ltx-production`, `pnpm test:whisperx`. Independent commands may run concurrently within their configured tier, never across tiers. Do not duplicate inherited validation commands in `.ai-orchestrator.json`. If adding a validation command, add its tier coverage.

Use the pinned installation/check scripts described in AGENTS.md for subsystem dependencies, especially FFmpeg before actual media tests; do not use a stray host version or start a physical GPU certification run. Integration requires Docker and uses the configured 900-second validation allowance. Record environmental failures separately from code failures and never claim unexecuted checks passed.

Software completion requires typed pre-GPU denial for all unauthorized/mismatched inputs, tested eligible staging with isolated authentic-signature fixtures, no longer-to-124 fallback, unchanged legacy execution/fingerprint/provenance behavior, measured-output validation and exact timeline checks, and passing applicable validation. Enabling an actual longer profile remains conditional on externally supplied #445 acceptance plus an authorized staging grant; ordinary production promotion and physical certification remain #428 work. No expected output belongs under `certification/`, `baseline/` or `config/render-profiles/`.

+export function parseAllowedExecutionScopes(

+  for (const item of items) {

+      throw new WorkerConfigError(

+      );
+    }
+    if (!validScopes.includes(item as ExecutionScope)) {
+      validScopes.push(item as ExecutionScope);
+    }
+  }
+  return Object.freeze(validScopes);

+        `Candidate provenance frames ${reportProv.frames} does not match candidate specification frames ${candidate.specification.frames}`,
+        "FRAME_COUNT_MISMATCH"
+      );
+    }
+    if (
+      reportProv.width !== candidate.specification.width ||
+      reportProv.height !== candidate.specification.height
+    ) {
+      throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+        `Candidate provenance dimensions ${reportProv.width}x${reportProv.height} do not match candidate specification dimensions ${candidate.specification.width}x${candidate.specification.height}`,
+        "GEOMETRY_MISMATCH"
+      );
+    }
+    if (reportProv.route !== candidate.specification.route) {
+      throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+        `Candidate provenance route "${reportProv.route}" does not match candidate specification route "${candidate.specification.route}"`,
+        "ROUTE_MISMATCH"
+      );
+    }
+    if (reportProv.routingMode !== candidate.specification.routingMode) {
+      throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+        `Candidate provenance routingMode "${reportProv.routingMode}" does not match candidate specification routingMode "${candidate.specification.routingMode}"`,
+        "ROUTING_MODE_MISMATCH"
+      );
+    }
+    if (reportProv.workflowHash !== candidate.specification.workflowHash) {
+      throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+        `Candidate provenance workflowHash "${reportProv.workflowHash}" does not match candidate specification workflowHash "${candidate.specification.workflowHash}"`,
+        "WORKFLOW_HASH_MISMATCH"
+      );
+    }
+    for (const [modelKey, expectedHash] of Object.entries(candidate.specification.modelHashes)) {
+      if (modelKey === "additionalModels") {
+        if (typeof expectedHash === "object" && expectedHash !== null) {
+          for (const [addKey, addHash] of Object.entries(expectedHash)) {
+            if (reportProv.modelHashes[addKey] !== addHash) {
+              throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+                `Candidate provenance additional model hash for "${addKey}" mismatch: expected "${addHash}", got "${reportProv.modelHashes[addKey]}"`,
+                "MODEL_HASH_MISMATCH"
+              );
+            }
+          }
+        }
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (modelKey === "turboLora" && expectedHash === "none") {
+        continue;
+      }
+      if (reportProv.modelHashes[modelKey] !== expectedHash) {
+        throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+          `Candidate provenance model hash for "${modelKey}" mismatch: expected "${expectedHash}", got "${reportProv.modelHashes[modelKey]}"`,
+          "MODEL_HASH_MISMATCH"
+        );
+      }
+    }
+
+    // 8. Load workflow file & recheck hash
+    const candidateWorkflowPath = resolve(
+      comfyUiDir || DEFAULT_REPO_ROOT,
+      candidateProvenanceReport.workflow.relativePath
+    );
+    const rawWorkflow = await readWorkflowFileFn(candidateWorkflowPath);
+    const recheckedWorkflowHash = hashWorkflowFn(rawWorkflow);
+
+    if (
+      recheckedWorkflowHash !== candidate.specification.workflowHash ||
+      recheckedWorkflowHash !== candidateProvenanceReport.workflow.sha256
+    ) {
+      throw new WorkflowHashMismatchError(
+        `Workflow hash mismatch for candidate "${candidateKey}": rechecked "${recheckedWorkflowHash}", expected "${candidate.specification.workflowHash}"`
+      );
+    }
+
+    // 9. Authoritative license routing guard evaluated BEFORE any external I/O
+    const licenseComponentId =
+      H3_CANDIDATE_LICENSE_COMPONENT_BY_ROUTE[candidate.specification.route];
+    if (!licenseComponentId) {
+      throw new CandidateExecutionMismatchError(
+        `Candidate profile "${candidateKey}" has unrecognized route "${candidate.specification.route}" with no corresponding license-registry component`,
+        "UNLICENSED_CANDIDATE_ROUTE"
+      );
+    }
+    if (deps?.enforceLicenseRouting) {
+      deps.enforceLicenseRouting.enforce({
+        requiredComponents: [
+          {
+            componentId: licenseComponentId,
+            componentType: "model",
+            versionOrRevision: H3_CANDIDATE_LICENSE_COMPONENT_VERSION
+          }
+        ],
+        operation: {
+          kind: "generation",
+          renderJobId: job.jobId,
+          sceneId: job.sceneId
+        }
+      });
+    } else if (
+      deps?.useCase &&
+      "enforceLicense" in deps.useCase &&
+      typeof deps.useCase.enforceLicense === "function"
+    ) {
+      deps.useCase.enforceLicense({
+        renderJobId: job.jobId,
+        sceneId: job.sceneId,
+        renderProfileKey: candidate.key,
+        renderProfileVersion: candidate.version,
+        engine: candidate.specification.route === "i2v" ? "minimax_h3_i2v" : "minimax_h3_ref2v"
+      });
+    }
+
+    // 10. Conditioning and ShotPlan route constraints
+    let resolvedCandidateMedia: ResolvedApprovedVisualProductionMedia | undefined;
+    let stagedReferenceImage: StagedComfyUiInput | undefined;
+    let stagingFilename: string | undefined;
+    let canonicalRefs: readonly CanonicalReferenceEntry[] = [];
+
+    const stagedRefInputs: StagedComfyUiInput[] = [];
+    const manifestRefImages: ManifestReferenceImageEntry[] = [];
+    const stagedRefPaths: string[] = [];
+    let promptToInject = validatedInjected.prompt;
+    let executedInstruction: ManifestExecutedInstruction | undefined;
+    let previsReviewEvidence: ManifestPrevisReviewEvidence | undefined;
+
+    let executionError: unknown;
+    let executionResult: WorkerRenderOutput | undefined;
+    try {
+      if (isRef2v) {
+        // Reference-directed MiniMax-H3 execution
+        if (!deps?.shotPlanRepository) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "shotPlanRepository dependency is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+        if (!deps?.referenceAssetRepository) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "referenceAssetRepository dependency is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+        if (!validatedInjected.shotPlanId) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "injectedPayload.shotPlanId is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+        if (!validatedInjected.specRevision) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "injectedPayload.specRevision is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+
+        const shotPlanDomain = await deps.shotPlanRepository.findById(
+          validatedInjected.shotPlanId as ShotPlanId
+        );
+        if (!shotPlanDomain) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `ShotPlan "${validatedInjected.shotPlanId}" not found in shotPlanRepository`
+          );
+        }
+        const shotPlanDoc = shotPlanDomain.snapshot();
+
+        if (shotPlanDoc.status !== "approved") {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `ShotPlan "${shotPlanDoc.id}" must be approved, got status "${shotPlanDoc.status}"`
+          );
+        }
+        if (shotPlanDoc.sceneId !== job.sceneId) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `ShotPlan "${shotPlanDoc.id}" belongs to scene "${shotPlanDoc.sceneId}", but render job is for scene "${job.sceneId}"`
+          );
+        }
+        if (shotPlanDoc.specRevision !== validatedInjected.specRevision) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `ShotPlan "${shotPlanDoc.id}" specRevision ${shotPlanDoc.specRevision} does not match injected specRevision ${validatedInjected.specRevision}`
+          );
+        }
+        // Invariant: Ref2V shot plan cannot be executed on I2V candidate; ShotPlan routingMode must match
+        if (shotPlanDoc.routingMode !== "reference_directed") {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `ShotPlan "${shotPlanDoc.id}" routingMode must be "reference_directed", got "${shotPlanDoc.routingMode}"`
+          );
+        }
+
+        if (!deps?.sceneRepository) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "sceneRepository dependency is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+
+        const sceneDomain = await deps.sceneRepository.findById(job.sceneId as SceneId);
+        if (!sceneDomain) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(`Scene "${job.sceneId}" not found in sceneRepository`);
+        }
+        const sceneSnapshot = sceneDomain.snapshot();
+        if (sceneSnapshot.specRevision !== validatedInjected.specRevision) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `Scene "${job.sceneId}" specRevision ${sceneSnapshot.specRevision} does not match injected specRevision ${validatedInjected.specRevision}`
+          );
+        }
+        if (!sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanId) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `Scene "${job.sceneId}" has no approvedShotPlanId; reference-directed execution requires current-scene ShotPlan approval`
+          );
+        }
+        if (sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanId !== validatedInjected.shotPlanId) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `Scene "${job.sceneId}" approvedShotPlanId "${sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanId}" does not match injected shotPlanId "${validatedInjected.shotPlanId}"`
+          );
+        }
+        if (
+          sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanRevision === undefined ||
+          sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanRevision === null
+        ) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `Scene "${job.sceneId}" has no approvedShotPlanRevision; reference-directed execution requires verified current-revision approval`
+          );
+        }
+        if (sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanRevision !== validatedInjected.specRevision) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `Scene "${job.sceneId}" approvedShotPlanRevision ${sceneSnapshot.approvedShotPlanRevision} does not match injected specRevision ${validatedInjected.specRevision}`
+          );
+        }
+
+        if (!deps?.campaignRepository) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "campaignRepository dependency is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+        const campaign = await deps.campaignRepository.findById(sceneSnapshot.campaignId);
+        if (!campaign || !campaign.clientId) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            `Campaign "${sceneSnapshot.campaignId}" not found or lacks clientId in campaignRepository`
+          );
+        }
+        const expectedClientId = campaign.clientId;
+
+        if (!deps.referenceAssetRepository.listBindingsBySceneId) {
+          throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+            "referenceAssetRepository.listBindingsBySceneId is required for reference-directed execution"
+          );
+        }
+
+        const rawAssets = await deps.referenceAssetRepository.listBySceneId(job.sceneId as SceneId);
+        const assetsById = new Map<string, DomainReferenceAsset>(rawAssets.map((a) => [a.id, a]));
+
+        const rawBindings = await deps.referenceAssetRepository.listBindingsBySceneId(
+          job.sceneId as SceneId,
+          {
+            specRevision: validatedInjected.specRevision
+          }
+        );
+
+        for (const binding of rawBindings) {
+          if (binding.sceneId && binding.sceneId !== job.sceneId) {
+            throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+              `SceneReferenceBinding for asset "${binding.referenceAssetId}" belongs to scene "${binding.sceneId}", which does not match job sceneId "${job.sceneId}"`
+            );
+          }
+          if (
+            binding.specRevision !== undefined &&
+            binding.specRevision !== validatedInjected.specRevision
+          ) {
+            throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+              `SceneReferenceBinding for asset "${binding.referenceAssetId}" has specRevision ${binding.specRevision}, which does not match injected specRevision ${validatedInjected.specRevision}`
+            );
+          }
+        }
+
+        canonicalRefs = canonicalizeReferenceBindings({
+          bindings: rawBindings,
+          assetsById,
+          expectedClientId,
+          expectedSceneId: job.sceneId
+        });
+
+        if (canonicalRefs.length > 0) {
+          if (!deps?.objectStorage) {
+            throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+              "objectStorage dependency is required for reference image staging"
+            );
+          }
+          if (!deps?.stageReferenceImage) {
+            throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+              "stageReferenceImage dependency is required for reference image staging"
+            );
+          }
+          const imageValidator = deps?.imageValidator ?? deps?.imageInspectionPort;
+          if (!imageValidator) {
+            throw new RenderJobExecutionError(
+              "imageValidator dependency is required for reference image staging"
+            );
+          }
+
+          for (const ref of canonicalRefs) {
+            if (ref.asset.clientId !== expectedClientId) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference asset "${ref.referenceAssetId}" client "${ref.asset.clientId}" does not match scene campaign client "${expectedClientId}"`
+              );
+            }
+
+            const refAssetSceneId = (ref.asset as { sceneId?: string }).sceneId;
+            if (refAssetSceneId && refAssetSceneId !== job.sceneId) {

+                `Reference asset "${ref.referenceAssetId}" belongs to scene "${refAssetSceneId}", which does not match job sceneId "${job.sceneId}"`
+              );
+            }
+
+            const stored = await deps.objectStorage.getObject(
+              { bucket: ref.asset.storageBucket, key: ref.asset.storageObjectKey },
+              { maxBytes: MAX_CANDIDATE_IMAGE_BYTES }
+            );
+            if (!stored || !stored.body || stored.body.byteLength === 0) {

+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" is missing or empty in storage`
+              );
+            }
+
+            const bytes = stored.body;
+            if (bytes.length < 8) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" buffer is too small to be a valid image`
+              );
+            }
+
+            const declaredMime = (ref.asset.mimeType ?? "image/png").toLowerCase();
+            const imageInfo = parseImageByteHeader(bytes);
+            if (!imageInfo) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" has unknown or unsupported image format magic bytes`
+              );
+            }
+            if (imageInfo.mimeType !== declaredMime) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" detected format "${imageInfo.mimeType}" does not match declared MIME "${declaredMime}"`
+              );
+            }
+            if (imageInfo.width <= 0 || imageInfo.height <= 0) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" must have positive dimensions`
+              );
+            }
+            if (ref.asset.width !== undefined && imageInfo.width !== ref.asset.width) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" width mismatch: expected ${ref.asset.width}, got ${imageInfo.width}`
+              );
+            }
+            if (ref.asset.height !== undefined && imageInfo.height !== ref.asset.height) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" height mismatch: expected ${ref.asset.height}, got ${imageInfo.height}`
+              );
+            }
+
+            const actualSha256 = await hashBytesPort.hashBytes(stored.body);
+            if (actualSha256 !== ref.asset.contentHashSha256) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image sha256 mismatch for asset "${ref.referenceAssetId}": expected "${ref.asset.contentHashSha256}", got "${actualSha256}"`
+              );
+            }
+
+            let inspected: ValidatedImageMetadata;
+            try {
+              inspected = await imageValidator.inspectAndValidate(bytes, declaredMime);
+            } catch (cause) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" decode validation failed: ${(cause as Error).message}`,
+                { cause }
+              );
+            }
+
+            if (inspected.detectedMimeType !== declaredMime) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError(
+                `Reference image object "${ref.asset.storageObjectKey}" detected format "${inspected.detectedMimeType}" does not match declared MIME "${declaredMime}"`
+              );
+            }
+
+            const refStagingFilename = buildDeterministicStagingFilename(
+              job.sceneId,
+              `${job.jobId}-slot${ref.slotIndex}`,
+              actualSha256,
+              ref.asset.mimeType ?? "image/png"
+            );
+            if (refStagingFilename.includes("..")) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError("refStagingFilename contains path traversal");
+            }
+
+            const stagedInput = await deps.stageReferenceImage.stage({
+              filename: refStagingFilename,
+              bytes: stored.body,
+              contentType: ref.asset.mimeType ?? "image/png"
+            });
+            if (
+              stagedInput.name.includes("/") ||
+              stagedInput.name.includes("\\") ||
+              stagedInput.name.includes("..") ||
+              (stagedInput.subfolder &&
+                (stagedInput.subfolder.includes("..") ||
+                  stagedInput.subfolder.startsWith("/") ||
+                  stagedInput.subfolder.startsWith("\\")))
+            ) {
+              throw new ReferenceImageIntegrityError("stagedInput contains path traversal");
+            }

+

+              ? `${stagedInput.subfolder}/${stagedInput.name}`
+              : stagedInput.name;
+            stagedRefPaths.push(stagedPath);
+
+            const injectionTarget = topology.referenceImages![ref.slotIndex - 1]!;
+            manifestRefImages.push({
+              bindingId: ref.bindingId,
+              slotIndex: ref.slotIndex,
+              promptTag: ref.promptTag,
+              assetId: ref.referenceAssetId,
+              contentHashSha256: actualSha256,
+              role: ref.role,
+              stagedAs: { name: stagedInput.name, subfolder: stagedInput.subfolder },
+              injectionTarget: {
+                nodeId: injectionTarget.nodeId,
+                classType: injectionTarget.classType,
+                inputField: injectionTarget.inputField
+              }
+            });
+          }
+        }
+
+        const sceneSpec = {
+          revision: validatedInjected.specRevision,
+          actionContext: sceneSnapshot.configuration?.prompt,
+          scriptContext: (sceneSnapshot as { scriptContext?: string }).scriptContext
+        };
+
+        const compiled = compileShotPlan({
+          shotPlan: shotPlanDoc,
+          sceneSpec,
+          references: canonicalRefs,
+          routingMode: "reference_directed"
+        });
